messages.subject: permutation using CIM
parts:
Dear Rqtl users,
I run a permutation procedure using the cim() function but obtained
strange results. Actually, I get 90% of the LOD score values < 5 and
about 10% > 250 ! So, when asking for a LOD threshold for alpha =
0.05, I get about 250 and all the previously detected QTL appear non
significant.
I guess having so much LOD > 250 is unlikely as well as having a non
continuous distribution (there's no intermediate values between 5 and
250) Have anyone experienced such strange results ?
This may come from my dataset so I can provide the source files if
needed .
Thanks for your help
Matthieu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] permutation using CIM
parts:
This is probably the case of spurious peaks that occurs with standard interval mapping when the phenotype is not very normally distributed and there are regions of low genotype information (e.g., big gaps between markers). (See, for example, Fig 4.14 on page 97 in Broman and Sen, A guide to QTL mapping with R/qtl.)

The simplest solution is to use method="hk" (Haley-Knott regression) and/or transform the phenotype, perhaps by taking ranks and then converting to normal quantiles.

Here's a function to do the latter:

nqrank <- function(x)
{
y <- rank(x[!is.na(x)])
x[!is.na(x)] <- qnorm((y-0.5)/length(y))
x
}

then try

mycross <- transformPheno(mycross, pheno.col=1, transf=nqrank)

karl
